channels.label: SIGNAL
paragraphs: I build the worlds the camera believes in. Flats, facades, breakaways, rigs — scenic construction for film and television, from first drafting to final strike.
Twelve years on stages and locations. Comfortable in timber, steel, foam, and whatever the art director dreamed up at 2am.

projects.title: Period Storefront Facade
projects.desc: Full-scale 1940s high street exterior. Three storefronts, practical doors and glazing, aged brick finish over timber frame. Built in sections for a night shoot turnaround.
projects.caption: CAM 1

projects.title: Breakaway Wall Rig
projects.desc: Stunt-rated breakaway wall with resettable panels, engineered for six takes. Balsa core, scored plaster skin, hidden steel safety frame.
projects.caption: CAM 2

projects.title: Rotating Stage Platform
projects.desc: 24-foot motorized turntable for a single-take musical number. Steel chassis, silent drive, deck dressed as a diner interior.
projects.caption: CAM 3

projects.title: Late Night: The Miniature Hour
projects.desc: 1:8 scale city block for a destruction sequence. Cast plaster buildings with frangible cores, wired for pyro cues.
projects.caption: CAM 4

steps.text: Every build starts on paper — or these days, on screen. Working drawings from the art department get translated into cut lists, material orders, and a build schedule that survives contact with the shooting calendar.
Framing, skinning, finishing. The trick is building something that reads as a hundred years old but comes apart in an afternoon. Wild walls, removable ceilings, everything labeled for the truck.
steps.caption: SHOP FLOOR — DAY 12

steps.text: On set for the shoot days — pulling walls between setups, resetting breakaways, keeping the standby carpenter's kit within arm's reach of the first AD.
What took three weeks to build comes down in two days. Materials sorted for salvage, stage swept, on to the next one.
